clue.text: Whimsical statistician embracing imaginary number

indicators.note: the statistician holds the number inside, as arms wrap round someone

parts.note: a quant is a quantitative analyst, a numbers specialist in finance
i is the mathematical symbol for the square root of minus one

explanation.surface: A quirky statistician gets fond of an imaginary number.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint describes something oddly old-fashioned or fanciful, close in sense to whimsical.

clue.text: Amount of tobacco leading to scrap in sport

indicators.note: the tobacco word comes first and leads on to the scrap word

parts.note: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco
to ditch something is to scrap it

explanation.surface: A wad of chewing tobacco leads to a fight during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight but is the verb meaning discard.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidditch is the broomstick game in the Harry Potter books, a fictional sport.

clue.text: Almost none for tea, dished up — now?

definitions.text: Almost none for tea, dished up — now?

indicators.note: food dished up has been prepared and served, so the letters are rearranged
almost the whole word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains there's next to nothing for tea, served right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: afternoon is when tea is dished up.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon is the traditional British time for tea, so now would be teatime.

clue.text: Leaders in North American ring corrupting drug cop

indicators.note: the leaders are the opening letters of each following word

parts.note: the four opening letters of these words are picked out

explanation.surface: The bosses of a North American gang are bribing a narcotics officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics agent who pursues drug offences.

clue.text: Quits taking in tense happenings

indicators.note: the first word absorbs the second, so the abbreviation sits inside it

parts.note: to be quits is to be even, owing nothing either way

explanation.surface: Someone quits after things get tense, as events unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Events and happenings are both plain synonyms for occurrences.

clue.text: Ungainly TV set to change, with much showing-off

indicators.note: the letters are set up to change into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An awkward old television is going to be swapped, with lots of boasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like the television set, but belongs to the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vauntingly means boastfully, from vaunt, to brag.

clue.text: Rugby staff turning up in Belgian city

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reverses the letters to read bottom to top

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union
to staff is to man, provide with workers

explanation.surface: Rugby officials arrive in a Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a city in southern Belgium on the Meuse.

clue.text: Cavity in small ear bone, not canine

indicators.note: not means the canine letter is left out

parts.note: the incus is the anvil bone of the middle ear
C is the dental notation for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: A hollow in a tiny bone of the ear, which is no dog's tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow space in bone, especially in the skull.

clue.text: Pause to bury first of potatoes in furrow

parts.note: inter means to place a body in a grave

indicators.note: the potato initial goes inside the groove word

parts.note: a rut is a groove worn in the ground

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the vegetable word is used

parts.note: the potatoes word supplies its initial, p

explanation.surface: A gardener stops work to plant a seed potato in a furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt is to break off or halt something, as in making it pause.

clue.text: Endlessly suffer with Circle, District, Victoria, Central etc?

indicators.note: the suffer word loses its last letter

parts.note: to undergo is to suffer or endure
a round is a circle

explanation.surface: Commuters forever suffering on the Tube lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle, District, Victoria and Central are lines on the London Underground; Circle is also wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The named lines are routes of London's Tube network, so together they are examples of it.

clue.text: Sources for this writer will have them working with novel for a year

indicators.note: the sources are the starting letters of each word

indicators.note: letters set working are put to use in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author's sources will keep them busy writing a novel for a whole year.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelvemonth is an old word for a year, twelve months long.

clue.text: Sap courage of member of emergency troops?

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are sent to crisis zones
a man is a member of a team or force

explanation.surface: Fear saps the nerve of a peacekeeping soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A UN man is one of the blue-helmet peacekeepers, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to rob them of their nerve, making them lose courage.

clue.text: Daughter beside boat in shadow

parts.note: Noah's ark is the most famous boat of all

explanation.surface: A daughter sits beside a boat in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dark lacks light, as a place in shadow does.

clue.text: Exploits servant due to go off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant's notes exploit a pension about to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploits as a noun are daring deeds, the same thing as adventures.

clue.text: Apostle taking worship is one on a famous journey

indicators.note: the apostle takes the worship word after him

parts.note: St Paul was an apostle
to revere is to worship

explanation.surface: An apostle, given to worship, sets out on a famous journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere made the 1775 midnight ride to warn that British troops were coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere is remembered for his midnight ride on horseback, a celebrated trip in American history.

clue.text: You'll get best atmosphere around with upstairs room

indicators.note: the word for best surrounds the abbreviation for with

parts.note: top means the finest
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: A promise of fresh air and a fine upstairs room, like an estate agent's advert.
explanation.walkthrough: A two-pair, in old British usage, is a room up two flights of stairs; poker players know the phrase as a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-pair room is literally one reached by climbing two pairs of stairs, so it lies upstairs.

clue.text: Against eating rotten grapes

parts.note: v for versus, as in a fixture

indicators.note: rotten things have decayed, so the letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest against eating rotten grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' looks like a containment signal but is anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage is the year's harvest of grapes, or the wine made from them.

clue.text: An obsessive soldier besetting one person receiving regular payments

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the obsessive surrounds the numeral for one

parts.note: a nut is an obsessive fan
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A fanatical soldier hounds a pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuitant is someone who receives an annuity, a yearly sum paid out.

clue.text: Space for printer to include border round about? It's always around

indicators.note: the printer's space holds the other parts within it

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of spacing

indicators.note: the border word goes round the about word

parts.note: a verge is the edge of a road or lawn
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A printer needs room for a border running round the page.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen plant keeps its leaves all year, so it is present in every season.

clue.text: Noir writer omitting first officer with police dog?

parts.note: Raymond Chandler wrote hardboiled detective novels such as The Big Sleep

explanation.surface: A crime novelist leaves out the first chapter about a police dog handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog handler is the police officer who works with and controls a trained canine.

clue.text: Guys around US city returning for one medley

LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for for one is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: Men heading home to an American city, each with a medley.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture of varied things, which is what a medley is.

clue.text: Monarch losing heart, besieged by smaller group later

indicators.note: the monarch word drops its middle letter

parts.note: a queen is a monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch, faint-hearted, is later besieged by a breakaway band.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsequent means coming afterwards, which is what later describes.

clue.text: Word on the street is "Inclined to give away money"

indicators.note: the inclined word gives up the money word, losing those letters

parts.note: slanting means inclined
tin is an informal British word for cash

explanation.surface: Local gossip says someone is minded to donate money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal street language, the vernacular of ordinary speech.

clue.text: Marvellous actor's last in order of appearance

clue.text: Last character in Government to display energy

parts.note: z is the final letter of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Zing is lively vigour or zest, an informal word for energy.

clue.text: Political assistant's first to drop plan

parts.note: an aide is a politician's assistant

clue.text: Heroine of children's book in a story about college

indicators.note: the story word goes round the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A children's heroine appears in a tale about a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll was an Oxford don, so the college fits the surface nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is the girl at the centre of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, a classic children's book.

clue.text: Dry? Heated dry, roughly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate is to remove the water from something, which is to dry it.

clue.text: Valuable information about elderly
